label: Original-sequence reading phase through <DEL> (dense, builds up over input)
explanation: Dense feature (41% of steps, 97% of sequences). It is on while the original tokens are being read, from about the third input (t>=2) through the <DEL> step: 73% of activation mass is in the original phase and 17% at <DEL>. It never fires at t=0 and rarely at t=1. Rate rises with position, peaking at orig_idx 4-6 (rate ~0.87) and at <DEL> (0.79). The largest activations (max ~9.7) are at <DEL> in short sequences built from the consonants d,f,k,l,s,v,x,z, often starting with 0. Activation ramps up step by step over such tokens, and prev_tok/prev2_tok in that set has about 1.5x lift. The feature is weak in the copy phase (rate 0.19). There it shows up mostly as a small residual at the first copy step after <DEL>, plus scattered low activations later. It is less active on repeated tokens (in_first=0 has 0.6x lift). The predicate (phase<=1)&(t>=2) gets about 0.74 precision, 0.76 recall and 0.88 mass recall on dev. Its misses are low-magnitude copy-phase activations. Its false positives are original-phase steps in sequences of vowels, digits, or other letters that lack the d/f/k/v/s/l/x/z set. Adding a condition on having seen those consonants raised precision to 0.83 but lowered recall, so it was not kept.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (copy phase: 0, g, 2, y; input phase: e, x, z, d; delimiter step: <DEL>) and the previous input (most: f, d, k, v, s, l; least: 2, 0, g, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=4.
